name: MonarchSectionHeader
title: SectionHeader
wrapsNative: HStack and VStack of Text with the header trait, ProgressView; usable as the header of Section in a List
summary: The title of a section that has no box around it, with an optional description, a meta line, a busy indicator and trailing actions.
whenToUse: Above a group of content on a screen or inside a card, when the group needs a title and perhaps one or two actions. In a List, pass it as the header of a Section.
whenNotToUse: For the title of a screen use navigationTitle. For a plain uppercase list header the system Section("Title") is enough. For a boxed group use MonarchCard.
api: MonarchSectionHeader.init(_ title: String, description: String? = nil, meta: String? = nil, size: MonarchSectionHeaderSize = .sm, isBusy: Bool = false, busyLabel: String? = nil, @ViewBuilder actions: () -> Actions)

MonarchSectionHeader.init(_ title: String, description: String? = nil, meta: String? = nil, size: MonarchSectionHeaderSize = .sm, isBusy: Bool = false, busyLabel: String? = nil) where Actions == EmptyView

options.name: description
options.description: A sentence under the title that explains the section.

options.name: meta
options.description: A short secondary line: a count, a date range, "Updated 5 min ago".

options.name: size
options.description: sm: a 14-point title for dashboard sections and cards. md: a 16-point title for the sections of a screen.

options.name: isBusy
options.description: Whether the section's content is loading or refreshing. Shows a progress indicator after the title.

options.name: actions
options.description: Buttons, a menu or a link at the trailing edge. Omit it for a header without actions.

states.name: default
states.description: The title, then the description and the meta line when given, with the actions at the trailing edge on the title's row.

states.name: busy
states.description: A small system progress indicator follows the title, and the title's spoken value is "Loading".

states.name: accessibility text sizes
states.description: The actions move below the text, at the leading edge, so the title keeps the full width.

appearance: The title is semibold in the default text colour; the description and the meta line use the muted text colour, the meta line at caption size. Nothing is drawn behind the header, so it takes the background of its container in every theme.
platformNotes: The web component can also wrap the section's content (children) in a labelled section element and dims it while busy; on iOS the header is only the header, and the content follows it in the stack or in the List section. The web's headingLevel (h2 to h6) is not offered: the title has the header trait, which is what VoiceOver's Headings rotor uses. The web's separate link slot and SectionHeaderLink are the actions slot here, with a Button or Link in the monarchLink(.subtle) style and a chevron.forward icon. On the web the trailing part wraps under the text when the row is too narrow; here it moves below at the accessibility text sizes. Android ships the same parameters.
accessibility: The title has the header trait.
While isBusy is true the title's accessibility value is "Loading" or busyLabel, and the progress indicator is hidden from VoiceOver so the state is read once.
The description and the meta line are separate text elements, read after the title.
Each action stays its own element after the text.
Every text scales with Dynamic Type and wraps; nothing is truncated.
At the accessibility text sizes the actions are placed below the text.
edgeCases: A long title wraps beside the actions; the actions keep their natural width.
Many or wide actions leave the title little width at standard text sizes. Keep to one or two small buttons, or a Menu.
Inside a List section header the system may uppercase header text; add textCase(nil) to the header to keep the title as written.
isBusy does not dim or disable the section's content; the screen that owns the content does that.
